contributions.headingText: Tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity (TCCRP) is a rare subtype of invasive breast carcinoma characterized by tall columnar cells with reversed nuclear polarity, arranged in solid and solid papillary patterns, most commonly associated with IDH2 p.Arg172 hotspot mutations.
8509/3 Tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity
2C6Y Other specified malignant neoplasms of breast

Not recommended: solid papillary carcinoma with reverse polarity; breast tumour resembling the tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma; solid papillary carcinoma resembling the tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma.
There is no specific predilection for location in the breast.

These tumours present as a mammographic or palpable mass. Ultrasonography reveals a hypoechoic mass with or without posterior shadowing {19594763; 22313838}. Axillary lymph node metastases have been reported in 3 patients {16501842; 17172492; 28418993; 30308500}.
No specific epidemiological data are currently available. All of the reported patients are women, with a mean age of 64 years (range: 39–89 years) {28418993; 29785016; 29603332; 30227763}.

TCCRP is characterized by IDH2 p.Arg172 hotspot mutations, which have been reported in about 84% (32 of 38) of the cases studied {28375433; 29785016; 29603332; 30227763; 27913435}. Hotspot mutations affecting IDH2 have been described in glioma, acute myeloid leukaemia, chondrosarcoma, and cholangiocarcinoma, but they are extremely rare in breast carcinomas other than TCCRP {29785016; 27913435}. PIK3CA missense mutations have been identified in about 68% (26 of 38) of these tumours {28375433; 29785016; 29603332; 30227763}, although mutations affecting PI3K pathway–related genes are quite common in breast cancer. There is no difference in the frequency of PIK3CA mutations in cases with and without IDH2 mutations {28375433; 29785016; 29603332; 30227763; 27913435}. BRAF mutations and RET/PTC rearrangement, which are molecular features of papillary thyroid carcinoma, have been negative in the TCCRP cases studied {19543246}.

TCCRP most often presents as a well-circumscribed, firm, white to grey mass {17172492; 24868004; 29785016}. The tumours range in size from 0.6 to 5 cm, with a median size of 1.5 cm {28418993; 29785016; 29603332; 30227763}.

TCCRP is composed of circumscribed nests of epithelial cells, most often distributed in dense fibrous stroma. Many of the nests have delicate fibrovascular cores, imparting a solid papillary pattern. Foamy histiocytes are often present within the fibrovascular cores. True papillae and cystic structures containing colloid-like material can be observed in some cases. The neoplastic nests are surrounded by a thin rim of capillary vessels. The tumour cells are tall and columnar, with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. Most cases show bland, round to ovoid nuclei, with variable presence of nuclear grooves and intranuclear cytoplasmic inclusions {12883243}. The most striking histological feature of TCCRP is the presence of nuclei at the apical rather than basal poles of the columnar epithelial cells. Mitotic figures are rare {28418993; 29785016; 30308500; 30227763}. Although TCCRP shows some histological similarities to the tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma, immunohistochemical and molecular studies confirm the breast origin of this tumour {28418993; 29785016; 30308500; 30227763}.

Most TCCRPs have a triple-negative phenotype, and the remaining cases show weak or focal hormone receptor expression {17172492; 27913435; 28418993; 29603332; 29785016; 30227763; 30308500}. Almost all reported cases are ERBB2 (HER2)-negative {28418993; 29785016; 29603332; 28375433}. The Ki-67 proliferation index is usually low (< 20%). These lesions characteristically express both low- and high-molecular-weight cytokeratins, as shown with CK7 and CK5/6 immunostaining, respectively. Chromogranin A and synaptophysin are consistently negative. Myoepithelial cells are not present around the tumour cell nests of TCCRP. In a study of 9 cases, all showed positive calretinin expression (with strong diffuse staining or focal staining) {29785016}. An origin in the breast is supported by variable staining for GCDFP-15, GATA3, and mammaglobin, along with a lack of staining for NKX2-1 (thyroid transcription factor 1) and thyroglobulin. Immunohistochemistry with antimitochondrial antigen shows condensation of mitochondria in the basal pole of the cells {28418993}.

Essential: an invasive breast carcinoma with the neoplastic cell nests arranged in a predominantly solid papillary pattern, composed of columnar epithelial cells showing reversed polarity of the nuclei; absence of myoepithelial cells around the tumour nests.

Desirable: expression of both low- and high-molecular-weight cytokeratins; a triple-negative or weakly hormone receptor–positive phenotype.
Cases should be staged according to the criteria for invasive breast carcinoma.

TCCRP has an indolent clinical course, with a favourable prognosis. The majority of patients have been disease-free during the follow-up period (range: 3–132 months) {28418993; 29785016; 28375433; 29154377}. Only one case with aggressive clinical behaviour (bone metastases) has been reported {16501842}.
